subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core shell-facing admin notification surface now, fold this into the broader WebUI notification architecture, or leave shell-originated alerts to plugin/external delivery paths?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent, but implementing it creates a new admin-scoped path from shell scripts into connected UI clients and needs maintainer intent on security boundary, UI interruption policy, and ownership before code work.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Notifications
options.body: Make the broader WebUI notification-system issue own the UI architecture and supersede this only after it explicitly covers shell/admin broadcast.

options.title: Prefer Plugin Or External Delivery
options.body: Reject a core command and document the supported plugin, channel, or Web Push workaround if maintainers decide shell-originated alerts should not directly interrupt Control UI sessions.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main central surfaces and recent blame point to Peter as the best available coordinator for the CLI/Gateway/UI boundary choice.
